findings.reason: Confirmed; filed as high, I would grade it medium. L14 is marked library with tauceti:…AbelianVariety.IsIsogeny and isIsogeny_iff. At Tau Ceti f790474 (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/Isogeny.lean) these declarations define an isogeny of abelian varieties over a field K as a morphism whose underlying scheme map is finite and surjective. L14's statement, however, is the §2.3.1 construction (author PDF pp. 30–31). It defines Hom_Q(A_{s₀}, A_{s₀′}) as a Q-scheme with R-points R ⊗ Hom, and R-isogenies as its invertible points for a coefficient Q-algebra R. Neither declaration supplies this. Its API (finite-surjective criterion, field base change) and its tests concern the geometric notion. So the library status is wrong for the statement as written. I would grade it medium rather than high: T26 already states and plans the rational Hom-scheme construction as missing, so nothing is lost from the plan, and the error is a status, not a false statement. The fix is right: restrict L14 to the geometric predicate the declarations supply, and leave the coefficient-algebra definition to T26 on its A6 route.

Confirmed (high). The author PDF (§2.2.6, p. 26; SHA-256 fd22990b…52db, equal to the extraction's) calls W admissible 'if it is a multiple of' a listed representation, with no positivity. T18 says 'a positive multiple'. T19(ii) requires that for every character χ: Z_G → G_m over Q̄ the χ-part of V is admissible. Z_G contains the scalar weight torus, so it has infinitely many characters, while V has finitely many central weights. For any absent χ the χ-part is 0, which is not a positive multiple of a nonzero representation. Read together, T18 and T19 therefore make condition (ii) fail for every type-D^R datum, and the definition of strictly accommodating excludes the whole D^R case. The fix is right: allow multiplicity zero for character parts, or quantify (ii) over the characters that occur in V.

Confirmed (high). The page image of p. 26 shows the square with downward vertical arrows and the right-hand arrow (G_V, H_V) → (∏ G_{V_j}, ∏ H_{V_j}), where G_V = GSp(V), and T19 copies it. A symplectic decomposition V ≅ ⊕ V_j gives no map GSp(V) → ∏ GSp(V_j). The red team's block swap on Q² ⊕ Q² with J ⊕ J lies in GSp(V) but does not preserve the summands. Reversing the arrow fails too: diag(2I₂, I₂) ∈ GSp₂ × GSp₂ has multipliers 4 and 1, so it pulls J ⊕ J back to 4J ⊕ J, which is not a scalar multiple, and it is not in GSp(V). The well-typed form uses the equal-multiplier subgroup ∏_{G_m} GSp(V_j) ⊂ GSp(V), with G → ∏ G_j and V = ⊕ V_j as G-representations. That matches the paper's remark that the notion agrees with Noot's. E4 corrects only the word 'accommodating' in the same definition; E5 and E32 concern pp. 28 and 27. The fix is right, including a new source issue scoped to the author copy.

Confirmed (medium). E5's accepted correction takes X′ to be 'the G′(R)-orbit of (h_0, h_T); X × {h_T} can be a finite union of such orbits'. T23.proofSteps[0] still takes X′ = X × {h_T} and asserts an embedding of Shimura data (G′, X′). The red team's example is right. For G = GL₂ = GSp₂ and T an imaginary-quadratic torus, G′ = GL₂ ×_{G_m} T over det and the norm. On real points the norm is |t|² > 0, so G′(R) maps into GL₂⁺(R), which preserves each half-plane of X = ℍ^±. So X × {h_T} has at least two G′(R)-orbits. The fix, propagating E5's orbit choice into the proof steps and specifying the component used in the lifting step, is right. This is not a new erratum.
